provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The input is a lattice of 3x3 tiles. Separator rows and columns sit at indices that are multiples of 4, and the grid size is (4h+1)x(4w+1). Every D4 transform maps an index i to either i or (4k - i). So separator rows and columns stay at multiples of 4, and tile cells stay at offsets 1-3 mod 4 on both axes. This holds even when a rotation swaps the height and width of a rectangular grid. The emitted program therefore walks the 3x3 windows starting at rows/columns 1, 5, 9, ... in visible coordinates. Inside each window it inverts the tile: a foreground cell (palette[8]) becomes background (palette[0]), and every other cell (the background) becomes the new colour (palette[2]). Separator cells keep their background colour. The colour roles are fixed constants taken from the palette.
draft_notes.limitations: Colour roles are set from the palette constants, not inferred from the demos. This assumes the generator's domain: tile cells are only background or foreground, and the grid dimensions are 4k+1. Inside a tile, any cell that is not the foreground colour is turned into the new colour, which matches the archived solver. No contradictions with the fixtures were noticed. Nothing has been tested; I did not run anything.
